text: What did Jesus write in the dirt of the temple floor in the story of the woman taken in adultery? Hey everybody, I'm Dan Mlelen. I'm a scholar of the Bible
and religion. And the answer is a very simple one. Nothing. Because this didn't happen. This is a literary creation.
There is no historical event behind what is in the text. All that matters is what is in the text. And so there is nothing
that was written in the dirt of the temple floor. But I want to suggest that there is symbolism just in the notion of
Jesus riding in the dirt of the temple floor because we've got a story of a woman who is caught in the act of
adultery and is taken to the temple to see if Jesus who is God's avatar or
representative on earth will condemn her to death. And the closest conceptual analog that we have to this anywhere in
the scriptures is in numbers five. What is known as the sot or the ordeal of bitter waters. And the idea here is that
if a man suspects his wife is guilty of adultery but has no evidence, he takes
her to the temple, presents her before the priest with an offering, and he writes a curse out, and then takes a jug
of water, takes some dirt from the temple floor, tosses it in the water,
scrapes the ink of the curse off into the water, and then the woman pronounces a blessing or a curse on her, depending
on her guilt or innocence and drinks the water. And then if she is innocent, she will conceive. She will be blessed with
fertility. If she is guilty, she will be cursed with infertility. And that is represented by these uh grotesque disformationations of her genitals,
which is imagery that is associated with infertility in ancient West Asia. And so I would suggest that one way to think
about this story, it may not have been what the author was intending, but we have many of the elements of the sot.
And so Jesus is being presented with a case of a woman not suspected of adultery, but caught in the actual act.

when given an even more clear case of adultery, Jesus refuses to condemn the
